expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: "No, that test would not have caught this incident"

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: "Coalescing a join-miss to 0 converts 'I don't know this value' into 'this value is zero' — a normal, plausible-looking number. That's the design choice that let three weeks pass."

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: "Reconciliation check ('does it agree?'): sum of revenue in your table vs. a source-of-truth total (billing system, upstream table row sum)"

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: No mention of pre-publication assertion timing; discusses 'loud failure same-day' but not publication blocking

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: No data contract or schema check mentioned

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: "Null-rate assertion on the joined column, pre-coalesce" and "Volume check with a floor"

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Discusses what would catch the incident but not the three-week gap as a systemic failure

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: Contrasts failure modes but does not explain the relative danger compared to loud failures
